originalTitle: Ariana Grande is suing the hackers who’ve been leaking her songs and videos for years
summary: Ariana Grande filed a lawsuit on Monday in the Los Angeles County Superior Court against the currently unidentified hackers who allegedly stole and leaked private content. content: Ariana Grande filed a lawsuit on Monday in the Los Angeles County Superior Court against the currently unidentified hackers who allegedly stole and leaked private content. It aims to “uncover the identities of these currently unknown and unscrupulous individuals,” referred to as  “John Doe 1 and John Does 2 through 100.” The lawsuit also says that “In 2023 alone, 45 unreleased songs” were “hacked, stolen, and leaked,” adding that hundreds of similar leaks have happened since Grande’s music debut in 2011.  The stolen content is said to include “still-in-production, unreleased masters and demos, footage from recording sessions, music videos, behind-the-scenes photographs and videos, as well as album and photoshoot outtakes.”  The lawsuit accuses the unidentified hackers of selling the content, as well as publishing it on social media platforms like X, TikTok, and YouTube. It claims their actions are invading her privacy and violating California’s Comprehensive Data Access and Fraud Act, a law against unauthorized computer access that has come up in cases including Sony’s lawsuit against George Hotz and Meta’s lawsuit against the Pegasus spyware. As reported earlier by Variety, the lawsuit claims the hackers have repeatedly targeted people who work with Grande. In one incident in 2019, hackers stole Grande’s photos from a photographer’s Dropbox account. The following year, unreleased footage was stolen from a producer’s hacked “mobile device.” In 2024, scammers used phishing emails to get unreleased photos from a technician working with one of Grande’s photographers.

chineseContent: 周一，爱莉安娜·格兰德 (Ariana Grande) 在洛杉矶县高等法院对涉嫌窃取和泄露私人内容的目前身份不明的黑客提起诉讼。它的目的是“揭露这些目前未知且肆无忌惮的个人的身份”，被称为“John Doe 1 和 John Doe 2 到 100”。该诉讼还称，“仅在 2023 年，就有 45 首未发行的歌曲”被“黑客攻击、窃取和泄露”，并补充说，自 Grande 2011 年首次亮相以来，已经发生了数百起类似的泄露事件。据说被盗的内容包括“仍在制作中、未发布的母带和演示、录音片段、音乐视频、幕后照片和视频，以及专辑和照片拍摄的片段”。  该诉讼指控身份不明的黑客出售这些内容，并将其发布在 X、TikTok 和 YouTube 等社交媒体平台上。它声称他们的行为侵犯了她的隐私，并违反了加州的《综合数据访问和欺诈法案》，该法案是一项禁止未经授权的计算机访问的法律，该法律在索尼针对乔治·霍茨的诉讼和梅塔针对 Pegasus 间谍软件的诉讼等案件中都出现过。正如 Variety 早些时候报道的那样，该诉讼声称黑客多次针对与 Grande 合作的人员。在 2019 年的一次事件中，黑客从一名摄影师的 Dropbox 帐户中窃取了 Grande 的照片。第二年，未发布的视频从制片人被黑的“移动设备”中被盗。 2024 年，诈骗者利用网络钓鱼电子邮件从与 Grande 的一位摄影师合作的技术人员那里获取未发布的照片​​。
